reading.body:
CyrusOne Totowa publishes 6 MW of IT capacity across a two-building campus near Totowa, New Jersey, about 17 miles from Midtown Manhattan. The site comprises 50,000 square feet of data center space and 60,000 square feet of work area recovery space within 200,000 total square feet. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 6 MW of IT load is roughly 150 racks, though the operator's actual configuration is not published.

The campus holds SSAE 16 Type II certification, qualifying it for enterprises requiring audited security and availability controls. It ranks fourth by published capacity among five New Jersey facilities with disclosed megawatt figures, representing 5.4 percent of the state's 111.3 MW of published data center IT capacity. The state has 48 mapped facilities overall, most of which publish no capacity figures.

The site's proximity to Manhattan and integration into CyrusOne's National IX platform position it for New York metro enterprise and financial services tenants rather than large-scale AI training workloads. At 6 MW total, it is substantially smaller than the hyperscale campuses now driving US compute growth and grid constraint, and falls outside the scale at which individual facilities move national AI capacity trends.
